finish.subtitle: Can you guess it?
finish.cta: Did you guess it? Tell us below.
finish.intro: Can you finish what our elder started? The answer appears after the countdown.

episodes.start: A bargain you didn't need
episodes.end: is still money gone.

episodes.start: Marry the person who is kind
episodes.end: when nobody is watching.

episodes.start: Nobody on their last day wishes
episodes.end: they'd answered more emails.

episodes.start: Walk every day while you can, because one day
episodes.end: you'll wish you could.

episodes.start: Old friends are like old shoes:
episodes.end: they fit because you kept wearing them.

episodes.start: Watch how someone treats a waiter,
episodes.end: because that's who they really are.

episodes.start: No company will ever
episodes.end: love you back the way your family does.

episodes.start: Call your mother while you can, because one day
episodes.end: you'll give anything to hear her answer.

episodes.start: Most problems look smaller
episodes.end: after a good night's sleep.

episodes.start: Happiness is cheaper than you think:
episodes.end: a warm cup and good company.

episodes.start: Learn one new thing every year,
episodes.end: and you'll never feel old inside.

episodes.start: Holding a grudge is like
episodes.end: carrying stones up a hill for someone else.

episodes.start: Courage isn't feeling brave.
episodes.end: It's knocking while your hands still shake.

episodes.start: Money lost can be earned again,
episodes.end: but a lost afternoon is gone forever.

episodes.start: Never go to sleep angry.
episodes.end: Stay up and talk it through instead.

episodes.start: Your children won't remember what you bought them.
episodes.end: They'll remember the time you gave.

episodes.start: A lie saves you a minute
episodes.end: and costs you years of trust.

episodes.start: Say thank you often, because
episodes.end: nobody ever got tired of hearing it.

episodes.start: Getting old is a privilege
episodes.end: many never get. Enjoy every birthday.

episodes.start: A home isn't the walls.
episodes.end: It's who is waiting inside them.

episodes.start: The older I get, the less I want
episodes.end: and the richer I feel.

episodes.start: You learn nothing
episodes.end: while your own mouth is moving.

episodes.start: Even the longest winter
episodes.end: has always ended in spring.

episodes.start: Find work that matters to someone,
episodes.end: and you'll never feel useless.

episodes.start: Learn your neighbours' names, because
episodes.end: one day you'll need each other.

episodes.start: Falling down is part of life.
episodes.end: Staying down is a choice.

episodes.start: Rest isn't laziness.
episodes.end: It's how you keep going for eighty years.

episodes.start: Leave behind things that outlive you,
episodes.end: like recipes, stories and planted trees.

episodes.start: The world will change without asking you,
episodes.end: so learn to change with it.

episodes.start: The people we lose stay with us
episodes.end: in every habit they taught us.

thennow.cta: Then or now? Tell us below.
thennow.title_template: Then vs Now: {topic} | Ask The Elders #shorts
thennow.intro: How life has changed, and the lesson the elders take from it.
thennow.image_then: Authentic 1960s vintage photograph, faded film grain, warm sepia tones, of {scene}, candid, nostalgic, photorealistic, no text, no watermark
thennow.image_now: Modern candid photograph of {scene}, natural light, realistic colours, photorealistic, no text, no watermark, no logo

episodes.then_img: a young couple in 1960s clothes sharing a milkshake at a diner counter
episodes.now_img: a young person alone on a sofa at night looking at a dating app on a phone
pairs: He asked her father first.
He asks the group chat first.
Love letters took a week to arrive.
Messages arrive and get left on read.
You met at the dance hall.
You match with a photo.
episodes.lesson: The method changed. Showing up with your whole heart never did.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s family counting coins into labelled envelopes at a kitchen table
episodes.now_img: a person tapping a phone to pay at a modern coffee shop counter
pairs: We paid cash and felt every note leave.
We tap a card and feel nothing.
We saved up, then we bought it.
We buy it, then we pay it off.
Envelopes for rent, food and rainy days.
Apps that track everything but our habits.
episodes.lesson: Whatever the tools, spend less than you earn.

episodes.then_img: 1960s children playing ball in a quiet street at sunset
episodes.now_img: a child alone on a sofa lit by a tablet screen
pairs: Home when the streetlights came on.
Home all day, online all night.
One bike shared by four kids.
One tablet each.
Scraped knees and big stories.
Clean knees, fewer stories.
episodes.lesson: Let them get bored and muddy. That's where childhood lives.

episodes.then_img: a woman in the 1960s chatting on a rotary phone with a long cord in a hallway
episodes.now_img: a group of friends at a restaurant table all looking at their own phones
pairs: One phone in the hallway for the whole family.
Five phones at one dinner table.
You knew every friend's number by heart.
You can't remember your own.
Calls were short because they cost money.
Calls are free, and nobody makes them.
episodes.lesson: Call someone today. Your voice is a gift.

episodes.then_img: a grandmother kneading bread in a 1960s kitchen with flour on the table
episodes.now_img: a delivery rider handing a takeaway bag over at a front door at night
pairs: Sunday dinner took all morning to cook.
Dinner takes twenty minutes to arrive.
Recipes lived in Grandma's head.
Recipes live in a video.
Leftovers became Monday's lunch.
Leftovers go in the bin.
episodes.lesson: Cook one family recipe together. It's how love gets passed down.

episodes.then_img: a smiling 1960s factory worker in overalls holding a lunch tin at the factory gate
episodes.now_img: a tired young person working on a laptop in bed late at night
pairs: One job for forty years.
Four jobs in four years.
The whistle blew and work was over.
The laptop never really closes.
A gold watch when you retired.
A goodbye message in a group chat.
episodes.lesson: Work hard, then log off. Nobody gets a medal for burnout.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s shopkeeper wrapping groceries in brown paper behind a wooden counter
episodes.now_img: a hallway stacked high with cardboard delivery boxes
pairs: We fixed things until they fell apart.
We replace things before they break.
The shopkeeper knew your name.
The app knows your shoe size.
One good coat for ten winters.
Ten cheap coats in one winter.
episodes.lesson: Buy less, choose well, and make it last.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s family looking at a printed photo album together on a sofa
episodes.now_img: a person scrolling through thousands of photos on a phone
pairs: Twelve photos from the whole holiday.
Twelve hundred photos of one lunch.
We waited a week to see them.
We see them before we've lived it.
Albums on the shelf for the grandchildren.
Photos lost when the phone breaks.
episodes.lesson: Print your favourite photos. Your grandchildren will thank you.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s bride and groom cutting a simple cake in a church hall
episodes.now_img: a lavish modern wedding reception with fairy lights and a huge cake
pairs: A church hall, sandwiches and a borrowed dress.
A venue, a drone and a year of planning.
The whole street was invited.
The guest list has a spreadsheet.
The marriage was the big event.
The wedding is the big event.
episodes.lesson: Spend less on the day and more on the years after.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s family gathered around a small television in a cosy living room
episodes.now_img: a family on one sofa, each person watching a different screen
pairs: One TV, one channel, the whole family.
One sofa, five different screens.
You waited a week for the next episode.
You watch the whole season tonight.
Arguing over the aerial.
Arguing over the password.
episodes.lesson: Watch one thing together tonight. Laugh at the same moment.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s family loading suitcases onto the roof rack of a small car
episodes.now_img: a busy modern airport departure hall full of travellers on phones
pairs: A paper map and getting lost.
A blue dot that's never lost.
Postcards arrived after you got home.
Stories posted before you unpack.
One holiday a year, planned for months.
Weekend flights booked in minutes.
episodes.lesson: Get a little lost sometimes. That's where the stories are.

episodes.then_img: 1960s schoolchildren at wooden desks in front of a chalkboard
episodes.now_img: students in a modern classroom working on laptops and tablets
pairs: Chalk on a blackboard.
Slides on a smartboard.
Library books with a date stamp inside.
Answers in half a second.
Times tables chanted out loud.
A calculator in every pocket.
episodes.lesson: Easy answers are wonderful. Hard thinking is still your job.

episodes.then_img: 1960s neighbours walking to the shops carrying wicker baskets
episodes.now_img: a person on a gym treadmill watching a screen
pairs: We walked everywhere because we had to.
We pay to walk on a machine.
Dinner at six, bed by ten.
Snacks at midnight, scrolling till one.
Games outside until dark.
Step counts on a watch.
episodes.lesson: Walk somewhere today that you'd normally drive.

episodes.then_img: 1960s neighbours chatting over a garden fence beside a washing line
episodes.now_img: a modern apartment corridor with closed doors and parcels outside
pairs: You borrowed sugar from next door.
You don't know who lives next door.
Kids played in every garden.
Doorbells with cameras.
Someone always had your spare key.
Codes, apps and locked gates.
episodes.lesson: Knock on one door this week and say hello.

episodes.then_img: 1960s teenagers dancing around a record player in a living room
episodes.now_img: a teenager alone on a bus wearing big headphones
pairs: Saving for weeks to buy one record.
Every song ever, for a monthly fee.
Dancing in the living room together.
Dancing alone in your earbuds.
Playing a record until it wore out.
Skipping after ten seconds.
episodes.lesson: Play the song that made you happy at sixteen. Loudly.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s mother sewing a child's dress at a sewing machine
episodes.now_img: a huge pile of cheap new clothes heaped on a bed
pairs: Mended holes and patched elbows.
Holes come with the price tag.
Hand-me-downs from three cousins.
A new outfit for every photo.
Sunday best was one outfit.
Every day is a new outfit.
episodes.lesson: Learn to sew on a button. It saves more than money.

episodes.then_img: a man in the 1960s waiting at a bus stop reading a newspaper
episodes.now_img: an impatient person tapping a phone waiting for a page to load
pairs: Waiting weeks for a letter.
Annoyed when a page takes five seconds.
Film took a week to develop.
Photos are instant and forgotten.
Saving a whole year for a bike.
Next-day delivery feels slow.
episodes.lesson: Good things still take time. Let them.

episodes.then_img: 1960s grandparents telling stories to grandchildren beside a fireplace
episodes.now_img: smiling grandparents waving at grandchildren on a tablet video call
pairs: Three generations under one roof.
Three time zones on one video call.
Stories told by the fire.
Stories sent as voice notes.
Grandma lived down the road.
Grandma lives on the screen.
episodes.lesson: Distance changes. Calling every Sunday shouldn't.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s family holding hands around a simple dinner table
episodes.now_img: a person eating takeaway alone at a desk in front of a computer
pairs: Everyone at the table at six.
Everyone eats whenever they're hungry.
Saying thanks before the first bite.
Taking a photo before the first bite.
Nobody left until the plates were clean.
Half of it goes in the fridge.
episodes.lesson: Eat one meal a day with no screens. Just people.

episodes.then_img: a man in the 1960s fixing a car engine on a driveway
episodes.now_img: a modern electric car charging in a quiet street
pairs: Dad fixed the car on the driveway.
The car updates itself overnight.
Everyone could change a tyre.
Everyone calls for help.
Maps in the glovebox.
The car tells you where to turn.
episodes.lesson: Learn to fix one thing yourself. It builds a quiet confidence.

episodes.then_img: a man in the 1960s reading a thick book in an armchair by a lamp
episodes.now_img: a person scrolling short videos on a phone in bed
pairs: One book read slowly all winter.
A hundred videos before breakfast.
Reading until the lamp went out.
Scrolling until the battery dies.
Libraries packed on Saturdays.
Libraries quiet, and still free.
episodes.lesson: Read ten pages tonight instead of scrolling. Notice how you sleep.

episodes.then_img: a woman in the 1960s writing a letter with a fountain pen at a desk
episodes.now_img: a person typing a quick text message with one thumb
pairs: Three pages, written by hand.
Three letters: lol.
Kept in a shoebox for fifty years.
Deleted to free up space.
You chose every word.
Autocorrect chooses for you.
episodes.lesson: Write one handwritten note this month. It will be kept forever.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s woman hanging laundry on a washing line in a sunny garden
episodes.now_img: a couple folding laundry together in a bright modern flat
pairs: Monday was washing day, all day.
The machine does it while we sleep.
One person did every chore.
Chores are shared, or should be.
Sheets dried in the sunshine.
Sheets dried in a tumble dryer.
episodes.lesson: Share the work at home. It's the quietest kind of love.

episodes.then_img: a retired man in the 1960s tending vegetables on an allotment
episodes.now_img: an active older woman learning to paint in a bright modern art class
pairs: Retire at sixty-five and rest.
Retire at sixty-five and start something new.
The allotment was the whole plan.
Painting, travel, a new language.
Old age meant slowing down.
Old age means choosing what matters.
episodes.lesson: It's never too late to begin again.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s bedroom with a wind-up alarm clock and a book on the bedside table
episodes.now_img: a person in bed at 2am lit by a phone screen
pairs: A wind-up clock and a book.
A phone and a hundred alerts.
Lights out meant the day was done.
Lights out means the screen is on.
Eight hours of sleep was normal.
Eight hours sounds like a holiday.
episodes.lesson: Charge your phone outside the bedroom tonight.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s child happily opening one small wrapped present
episodes.now_img: a child surrounded by a mountain of opened presents looking bored
pairs: One orange at Christmas felt like treasure.
Twenty presents and bored by lunch.
A new pencil case was big news.
New things arrive every week.
We said thank you with a letter.
We say thanks with an emoji.
episodes.lesson: Fewer gifts, more gratitude. Children learn what we show them.

episodes.then_img: 1960s friends laughing together on a front porch with glasses of lemonade
episodes.now_img: a person alone on a sofa liking friends' photos on a phone
pairs: Friends dropped by without calling.
Friends need a calendar invite.
Five close friends you saw every week.
Five hundred followers you never see.
We argued, then made up the same day.
We argue, then quietly unfollow.
episodes.lesson: Visit a friend this week, unannounced, with cake.

episodes.then_img: two 1960s farmers shaking hands over a wooden fence
episodes.now_img: a person signing a long contract on a tablet with a stylus
pairs: A handshake was a contract.
A contract has forty pages.
Your word was your reputation.
Your reviews are your reputation.
The whole town knew if you lied.
The internet never forgets either.
episodes.lesson: Keep your word, even on small things. People remember.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s family watching a rocket launch on a black-and-white television
episodes.now_img: a family looking at the night sky through a telescope in a garden
pairs: We watched rockets and dreamed big.
We watch rockets on our phones.
The future felt exciting.
The future feels uncertain.
Every child wanted to be an astronaut.
Every child still looks up at the stars.
episodes.lesson: Keep looking up. The future still belongs to the curious.

episodes.then_img: a 1960s grandmother knitting in a rocking chair on a porch
episodes.now_img: a smiling grandmother in sportswear jogging in a park at sunrise
pairs: Seventy meant a rocking chair.
Seventy means a morning run.
Grey hair meant slowing down.
Grey hair means a new adventure.
Grandma knitted by the fire.
Grandma shows off her race medal.
episodes.lesson: Age is a number. How you spend the day is the story.
